phase: B4 data-quantity research, coarse data axis
registered_at_source: written before any scaling process started
purpose: Measure whether a materially larger training window improves out-of-sample RankIC at matched training amount, and whether it keeps paying between 240 and 450 trading days. Every earlier model in this project trained on 60 trading days; the data axis was never measured.
question: At matched effective epochs, how does out-of-sample RankIC move when the training window grows from 60 to 132 to 240 to 450 trading days?

data_availability.why_441_is_the_ceiling: the earliest trading day in the bar and label archives is 2022-01-04; 441 trading days ending 2023-10-31 is the largest window the data supports

known_deviation.clause: level 2 may only be considered after level 1 reaches the escalation state
known_deviation.deviation: the 240-day rung is run before the level-1 verdict is read
known_deviation.reason: the principal directed a broad data-quantity measurement for this compute window; the rung is run as curve estimation, not as escalation, and it cannot produce a candidate
mitigation: its windows, seeds, effective-epoch points and reading rules are fixed here, before any run
it may not be used to relax, overturn or pre-empt the level-1 C1 verdict
no promotion, no incumbent replacement and no sealed read follow from it

components.label: 240d
components.role: the provisional level-2 window that the level-1 document already named, run as a dose-response rung at matched effective epochs, paired by seed with the 60-day and 132-day rungs

components.label: 441d
components.role: the largest window this dataset supports: 2022-01-04 is the earliest trading day in the archive, so 441 trading days ending 2023-10-31 is the hard ceiling; the decisive rung for 'the model was always trained on too little data'

dose_response_design.fixed_axis: effective epochs (1.32 and 2.64) of one continuous trajectory per seed
dose_response_design.why_paired: the same three seeds are run on every rung, so the rung-to-rung difference is a paired difference and not a seed-lottery difference

declared_reading.primary: paired per-seed RankIC difference between adjacent rungs at 1.32 effective epochs
declared_reading.monotone_rule: declare 'more data pays' only when the seed-mean RankIC rises across at least three consecutive rungs and the 450-vs-132 paired difference has a 5-day block bootstrap interval whose lower bound exceeds zero
declared_reading.flattening_rule: declare 'more data stops paying' when the 450-vs-240 paired difference is negative or its interval straddles zero, while 240-vs-132 is positive
declared_reading.falsification_rule: if the 132-to-240 and 240-to-450 paired differences both straddle zero, the data-quantity hypothesis is reported as rejected at this resolution, and the next lever is feature and label information content, not more days
declared_reading.interval: the registered 5-day block interval, 4000 bootstrap draws, paired by trading day
declared_reading.trading_day_count_gate: before a rung starts, the measured trading-day count of its window must be within 2% of its declared count, otherwise the rung stops and reports

prohibitions: no promotion, no incumbent replacement, no candidate claim from any rung
no reading of the sealed interval
no change to any promotion threshold, secondary line, net5 limit or cost scenario
no re-selection of a window, seed or point after its value has been read
no reporting of a single seed as evidence for a rung
no use of this document to relax or overturn the level-1 C1 verdict
no run from this document before its own registration record exists
queue_rules: the rungs run only in free process slots and only when the measured pool peak allows it
each plan is one process and one uninterrupted trajectory
a failed process is retried at most once, then skipped and reported
partial completion is reported as partial
